dialogue:
JAMIE: Okay I am genuinely excited about this one. Alex, Rufus, picture your least favourite part of a workday. Not the hard stuff. The grind before the hard stuff.
ALEX: Oof. Reading back through a week of emails before a client call so you don't say something embarrassing.
RUFUS: Scrolling up through a CRM trying to remember what you promised someone three months ago.
JAMIE: YES. That. Financial advisors at RBC Wealth Management were spending over an hour per client just gathering and pulling together notes before each meeting. Not doing the meeting. Preparing for it.
ALEX: An hour. Per client. If you have eight meetings in a day that's an entire extra workday before the actual work starts.
JAMIE: Exactly the maths. So in March 2025 they deployed a Salesforce Agentforce AI agent. And the way it works is this: before a meeting, the agent goes into the advisor's Salesforce CRM in real time, pulls the client's account history, recent activity, relevant market context, synthesises all of it, and delivers a pre-meeting briefing. Autonomously.
JAMIE: The advisor didn't have to touch it.
RUFUS: How long does that take?
JAMIE: According to the Salesforce Agentforce vendor case study, meeting prep went from over an hour to under one minute.
RUFUS: Per client.
JAMIE: Per client.
ALEX: That's not an upgrade, that's a different category of thing entirely.
RUFUS: Hold on though. The agent is only reading the CRM. So if the CRM data is a mess, the briefing is a confident-sounding mess.
JAMIE: One hundred percent, and that is the real limitation here. Garbage in, polished garbage out. The accuracy of every briefing depends completely on how clean and current the underlying data actually is. So before you trust those summaries you need to trust what's feeding them.
ALEX: Which for a lot of teams means fixing the CRM first and that is not a small job.
RUFUS: So the AI saves an hour but data hygiene could cost you a month.
JAMIE: Which Rufus would know nothing about given the state of his shared folders.
RUFUS: My folders have a system.
ALEX: A system only Rufus understands is called a mystery.
JAMIE: But here is the useful bit for anyone listening. The workflow the agent performs is just a structured recurring task on top of existing data. That pattern works anywhere teams repeat the same preparation before the same type of meeting, whether that's client calls, account reviews, project check-ins.
ALEX: So what does a normal person actually do with this?
JAMIE: Pick one recurring meeting your team over-prepares for. Time how long that prep actually takes across your team in a week. Then trial an automated briefing agent against that specific task. If the output gives equivalent context, you have your answer.
JAMIE: And the Agentforce agent is available as a standard deployment within the Salesforce platform —
JAMIE: so for existing Salesforce shops there is no exotic build required. An hour of grind per client, down to a minute. That is a real shift in where skilled people put their attention.
